name: Noah
notable_events: Built the ark
Survived the flood
Sent out dove and raven
short_bio: Noah built the ark to survive the flood.

name: Moses
notable_events: Led the Israelites out of Egyptian bondage in the Exodus
Encountered the Lord at the burning bush on Mount Horeb
Parted the waters of the Red Sea by the power of God
Received the Ten Commandments inscribed on tablets of stone
short_bio: Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt.

name: Solomon
notable_events: Built the first magnificent temple of the Lord in Jerusalem
Was renowned throughout the ancient world for his God-given wisdom
Wisely judged between two mothers claiming the same baby
short_bio: Son of David and Bathsheba; famed for wisdom.

name: Joseph (son of Jacob)
age_notes: Sold by brothers at 17; died at 110
notable_events: Was sold into Egypt by his envious brothers
Interpreted Pharaoh’s prophetic dreams of famine and abundance
Stored grain and saved Egypt and surrounding nations from starvation
Forgave and lovingly reunited with his brothers in Egypt
short_bio: Joseph was sold into Egypt and rose to power.

name: David
notable_events: Defeated the Philistine champion Goliath with a sling and stone
Was anointed by Samuel and became king over all Israel
Danced joyfully before the Ark of the Covenant as it entered Jerusalem
Wrote many of the Psalms of praise and repentance
short_bio: Shepherd who became king of Israel; famous for defeating Goliath.

name: Esther
notable_events: Became queen of Persia and risked her life by approaching King Xerxes uninvited
Exposed Haman’s wicked plot and miraculously saved the Jewish people from destruction
short_bio: Jewish queen of Persia who saved her people.

name: Mary (mother of Jesus)
notable_events: Was visited by the angel Gabriel announcing the birth of the Messiah
Sang the Magnificat in joyful praise of God her Savior
Stood faithfully at the foot of the cross during Jesus’s crucifixion
short_bio: Mother of Jesus.

name: John the Baptist
notable_events: Baptized Jesus in the waters of the Jordan River
Preached repentance in the Judean wilderness wearing camel hair
Was imprisoned and martyred by King Herod
short_bio: Prophet who baptized Jesus.

name: Paul
notable_events: Was dramatically converted on the road to Damascus by a vision of the risen Christ
Undertook three major missionary journeys planting churches across the Roman Empire
Authored thirteen epistles forming a major portion of the New Testament
Surviving a shipwreck on the island of Malta
short_bio: Originally named Saul; became Apostle Paul after conversion.

name: Peter
notable_events: Stepped out of the boat and walked on water toward Jesus
Denied knowing Jesus three times before the rooster crowed
Preached with boldness at Pentecost leading 3,000 to faith
Saw the vision of the great sheet revealing the gospel was for Gentiles too
short_bio: One of Jesus's closest disciples; called Peter.

name: Lazarus
notable_events: Was raised from the dead by Jesus after four days in the tomb
Lived in Bethany as the beloved brother of Mary and Martha
short_bio: Brother of Mary and Martha; raised from the dead.

name: Abraham
notable_events: Fathered Isaac in his old age according to God’s covenant promise
Entered into the foundational covenant of circumcision with the Lord
Demonstrated supreme obedience by being willing to sacrifice Isaac on Mount Moriah
Left his homeland in Ur of the Chaldeans to journey to the Promised Land
short_bio: Father of the Israelite nation.

name: Isaac
age_notes: Died at 180; born when Abraham was 100
notable_events: Was born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age as the child of promise
Was bound upon the altar on Mount Moriah before God provided a ram
Married Rebekah and prayed for her to bear Jacob and Esau
short_bio: Son of Abraham and Sarah; father of Jacob.

name: Jacob
notable_events: Was renamed Israel after wrestling with the angel of the Lord until daybreak
Fathered the twelve sons who became the twelve tribes of Israel
Obtained Isaac’s patriarchal blessing with the help of his mother Rebekah
short_bio: Father of the 12 tribes of Israel.

name: Samuel
notable_events: Anointed both Saul and David as the first kings of Israel
Heard God’s voice calling his name in the temple as a young boy
Served faithfully as prophet and the final judge of Israel
short_bio: Prophet and judge who anointed Israel's first kings.

name: Elijah
notable_events: Was taken up to heaven bodily in a chariot of fire and a whirlwind
Confronted and defeated 450 prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel
Was miraculously fed bread and meat by ravens by the brook Cherith
Raised the widow of Zarephath’s son from the dead
short_bio: Great prophet who was taken to heaven in a chariot.

name: Jonah
notable_events: Was swallowed by a great fish after fleeing on a ship toward Tarshish
Preached a message of repentance that spared the great city of Nineveh
Waited angrily outside Nineveh under a gourd plant
short_bio: Prophet who fled God and was swallowed by a great fish.

name: Ruth
notable_events: Remained faithfully loyal to her mother-in-law Naomi, saying “Your God will be my God”
Gleaned in the fields of Bethlehem and married the kinsman-redeemer Boaz
Became the great-grandmother of King David in the lineage of the Messiah
short_bio: Moabite woman who became ancestor to King David.

name: Mary Magdalene
notable_events: Had seven demons cast out of her by Jesus and followed Him devotedly
Was the first witness to whom the risen Christ appeared on Resurrection morning
short_bio: Witness of Jesus's resurrection.

name: Saul (first king)
notable_events: Was anointed by Samuel as the very first king over the nation of Israel
Desperately consulted the medium of Endor on the eve of his final battle
Fell upon his own sword on Mount Gilboa after being defeated by the Philistines
short_bio: Israel's first king anointed by Samuel.

name: Daniel
notable_events: Was miraculously preserved unharmed in the den of hungry lions
Interpreted King Nebuchadnezzar’s mysterious dreams in Babylon
Read and explained the supernatural handwriting on the palace wall for Belshazzar
short_bio: Prophet in Babylon; survived lion's den.

name: Joshua
notable_events: Led the children of Israel across the Jordan into the Promised Land
Led the march around the city of Jericho until its fortress walls collapsed
Prayed for the sun to stand still in the sky during the battle of Gibeon
short_bio: Successor to Moses who led Israel into Promised Land.

name: Deborah
notable_events: Served as a prophetess and the only female judge leading Israel
Summoned Barak and directed the victory over the Canaanite general Sisera
Composed and sang a renowned victory hymn recorded in Judges 5
short_bio: Prophet and judge who led Israel to victory.

name: Gideon
notable_events: Defeated a vast Midianite army using only 300 men with trumpets and clay jars
Asked God for signs of confirmation using a fleece of wool
Tore down his father’s altar to Baal by night
short_bio: Judge who defeated the Midianites with 300 men.

name: Samson
notable_events: Tore apart a young lion with his bare hands through the Spirit of the Lord
Defeated a thousand Philistines armed with only the jawbone of a donkey
Was betrayed by Delilah who cut his hair and robbed him of his strength
Pulled down the pillars of the temple of Dagon in his final act of faith
short_bio: Judge with supernatural strength; betrayed by Delilah.

name: Jeremiah
notable_events: Wept over the spiritual rebellion and eventual fall of Jerusalem
Prophesied the coming of a New Covenant written on the human heart
Was cast into a muddy cistern for proclaiming God’s truthful warnings
short_bio: Weeping prophet who warned of Babylon's destruction.

name: Ezekiel
notable_events: Received the dramatic vision of the valley of dry bones coming to life
Saw the glorious vision of God surrounded by glowing wheels within wheels
Recorded detailed prophetic visions of the future restored temple
short_bio: Prophet of the exile with dramatic visions.

name: Isaiah
notable_events: Had his lips cleansed with a live burning coal from the heavenly altar
Authored profound prophecies detailing the Suffering Servant and the virgin birth
Responded to God’s call declaring: “Here am I! Send me.”
short_bio: Major prophet who prophesied about the Messiah.

name: Job
notable_events: Endured the sudden loss of his wealth, children, and health while remaining faithful
Declared with conviction: “I know that my Redeemer lives!”
Received double the blessings and livestock after praying for his critical friends
short_bio: Righteous man who suffered but remained faithful.

name: Nehemiah
notable_events: Led the rebuilding of the broken walls of Jerusalem in just 52 days
Served as royal cupbearer to King Artaxerxes before returning to Judah
Stood firm against hostile neighboring rulers who mocked the rebuilding effort
short_bio: Led rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.

name: Ezra
notable_events: Read and taught the Law of Moses aloud to the returned exiles in Jerusalem
Led a return of Jewish exiles from Babylon to restore temple worship
Fasted and prayed for God’s protection along the dangerous journey without soldiers
short_bio: Priest and scribe who restored the Law.

name: Adam
notable_events: Was the first man created by God from the dust of the ground
Named all the animals and birds placed in the Garden of Eden
Ate of the forbidden fruit with his wife Eve, bringing the Fall upon creation
short_bio: First human created by God.

name: Eve
notable_events: Was created by God from Adam’s rib as his companion and helper
Was deceived by the serpent in the Garden of Eden and ate the forbidden fruit
Was named the mother of all living humans
short_bio: First woman; mother of all humanity.

name: Cain
notable_events: Killed his righteous brother Abel in a field out of envy and anger
Was placed under a curse and marked by God to wander the earth as a fugitive
short_bio: First son of Adam and Eve; killed his brother.

name: Abel
notable_events: Offered the firstborn of his flock as an acceptable, faith-filled sacrifice to God
Was martyred by his older brother Cain, becoming scripture’s first murder victim
short_bio: Second son of Adam and Eve; murdered by Cain.

name: Lot
notable_events: Was rescued by angels before God rained brimstone and fire upon Sodom and Gomorrah
Fled to the town of Zoar while his wife looked back and became a pillar of salt
short_bio: Abraham's nephew who escaped Sodom's destruction.

name: Sarah
notable_events: Conceived and gave birth to Isaac at the age of ninety according to God’s promise
Laughed in disbelief when hearing she would bear a son in her extreme old age
Was honored in the New Testament as an enduring mother of faith
short_bio: Wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac.

name: Rebekah
notable_events: Drew water for Abraham’s servant Eliezer and his ten camels at the well
Gave birth to twin brothers Esau and Jacob who struggled in her womb
Helped her beloved son Jacob secure Isaac’s patriarchal blessing
short_bio: Wife of Isaac; mother of Jacob and Esau.

name: Rachel
notable_events: Was deeply loved by Jacob who worked fourteen years to marry her
Gave birth to Joseph and later died while giving birth to Benjamin
short_bio: Beloved wife of Jacob; mother of Joseph.

name: Leah
notable_events: Was Jacob’s first wife, given in place of her younger sister Rachel by Laban
Became the mother of six sons including Judah, the ancestor of the Messiah
short_bio: First wife of Jacob; mother of six of his sons.

name: Miriam
notable_events: Watched over baby Moses in his basket among the reeds of the Nile River
Led the Hebrew women in joyful singing and timbrel dance after crossing the Red Sea
Was temporarily struck with leprosy after questioning Moses’s sole authority
short_bio: Sister of Moses and Aaron; prophetess.

name: Aaron
notable_events: Served as the eloquent spokesman for his younger brother Moses before Pharaoh
Was consecrated as the very first High Priest of Israel
Owned the miraculous rod that budded, blossomed, and produced ripe almonds
short_bio: Brother of Moses; first high priest of Israel.

name: Caleb
notable_events: Was one of the two faithful spies who believed Israel could conquer the Promised Land
At age eighty-five boldly requested the hill country of Hebron and drove out the giants
short_bio: Faithful spy who trusted God's promise.

name: Elisha
notable_events: Received a double portion of Elijah’s prophetic spirit when Elijah was taken up
Healed the Syrian commander Naaman of his leprosy by instructing him to wash in the Jordan
Caused an iron axe head to float miraculously to the surface of the Jordan River
short_bio: Prophet who succeeded Elijah; performed many miracles.

name: Naomi
notable_events: Returned from the fields of Moab to Bethlehem in grief, calling herself “Mara”
Wisely guided her faithful daughter-in-law Ruth to seek redemption through Boaz
short_bio: Mother-in-law of Ruth; returned from Moab.

name: Boaz
notable_events: Showed remarkable kindness to the foreign widow Ruth gleaning in his barley fields
Redeemed Elimelech’s ancestral inheritance and took Ruth as his wife
short_bio: Wealthy man who married Ruth.

name: Hannah
notable_events: Wept bitterly in the tabernacle at Shiloh and vowed her unborn son to the Lord
Gave birth to Samuel and dedicated him to lifelong service under Eli the priest
Composed a renowned prayer of prophetic praise recorded in 1 Samuel 2
short_bio: Mother of Samuel; prayed faithfully for a son.

name: Eli
notable_events: Mentored young Samuel in the tabernacle and taught him how to answer God’s call
Failed to restrain his corrupt sons Hophni and Phinehas from desecrating the sacrifices
Died upon hearing that the Philistines had captured the sacred Ark of God
short_bio: High priest who mentored young Samuel.

name: Goliath
age_notes: Six cubits and a span tall (about 9 ft 9 in)
notable_events: Stood as the towering nine-foot champion of the Philistines defying Israel’s armies
Was struck down and slain by the shepherd youth David armed only with a sling
short_bio: Giant Philistine warrior defeated by David.

name: Jonathan
notable_events: Formed an unbreakable covenant of sacrificial friendship with David
Single-handedly scaled a cliff with his armor-bearer and routed a Philistine garrison
Fell heroically in battle alongside his father Saul on Mount Gilboa
short_bio: Son of Saul and loyal friend of David.

name: Bathsheba
notable_events: Was taken by King David while married to Uriah the Hittite
Became the queen mother of King Solomon and secured his throne
short_bio: Wife of Uriah then David; mother of Solomon.

name: Absalom
notable_events: Plotted a rebellion against his father David and proclaimed himself king at Hebron
Was caught by his long, beautiful hair in the thick branches of a great oak tree
short_bio: Son of David who rebelled against him.

name: Elkanah
notable_events: Father of Samuel
Husband of Hannah
short_bio: Father of Samuel; husband of Hannah and Peninnah.

name: Mordecai
notable_events: Cousin of Esther
Exposed assassination plot
Honored by king
short_bio: Cousin of Esther who helped save the Jews.

name: Joah
notable_events: Met the Assyrian field commander at Jerusalem's wall
Reported Rabshakeh's threats to Hezekiah
short_bio: Son of Asaph; recorder under King Hezekiah who met the Assyrian envoys.

name: Seth
notable_events: Born to replace Abel
His line called upon the name of the Lord
short_bio: Son born to Adam and Eve to replace Abel; father of Enosh whose line called upon the Lord.

name: Enosh
notable_events: In his days people began to call on the name of the LORD
short_bio: Son of Seth and grandson of Adam.

name: Kenan
notable_events: Son of Enosh and father of Mahalalel in the genealogy of Genesis 5
short_bio: Patriarch in the genealogy of Genesis 5, son of Enosh and father of Mahalalel.

name: Mahalalel
notable_events: Patriarch in the lineage from Adam to Noah, father of Jared
short_bio: Patriarch in the genealogy of Genesis 5, son of Kenan and father of Jared.

name: Jared
notable_events: Father of Enoch, lived 962 years in the line of Seth
short_bio: Father of the prophet Enoch, lived 962 years in the line of Seth before the flood.

name: Enoch (Jared's Son)
notable_events: 'Walked with God' and was taken away without seeing death
short_bio: Prophet and patriarch who walked faithfully with God and was taken to heaven without seeing death.

name: Methuselah
age_notes: Lived 969 years (Oldest man in the Bible)
notable_events: Lived to 969 years, the longest recorded lifespan in Scripture
Grandfather of Noah
short_bio: Patriarch who lived 969 years—the longest recorded lifespan in Scripture—and was Noah’s grandfather.

name: Lamech (Methuselah's Son)
notable_events: Named his son Noah, saying he would bring comfort
short_bio: Son of Methuselah and father of Noah.

name: Shem
notable_events: Ancestor of Abraham and the Israelites
short_bio: Oldest son of Noah who survived the great flood in the ark and became ancestor to Abraham and the Israelites.

name: Ham
notable_events: Saw his father Noah naked and was cursed (via his son Canaan)
short_bio: Son of Noah who survived the great flood in the ark, father of Cush, Mizraim, and Canaan.

name: Japheth
notable_events: Son of Noah who survived the Great Flood in the ark
Ancestor of maritime nations
short_bio: Son of Noah who survived the great flood in the ark, regarded as ancestor to the maritime nations.

name: Nimrod
notable_events: A mighty hunter before the LORD
Founded kingdoms including Babel and Nineveh
short_bio: Son of Cush; the first mighty warrior on earth.

name: Terah
notable_events: Father of Abraham
Traveled from Ur to Haran
short_bio: Father of Abraham, Nahor, and Haran who led his family on their initial journey from Ur toward Canaan.

name: Hagar
notable_events: Mother of Ishmael
Sent away into the wilderness twice
short_bio: Egyptian handmaiden to Sarah who became mother to Ishmael and was comforted by God in the wilderness.

name: Ishmael
notable_events: Sent away with Hagar into the wilderness
Father of twelve princes
short_bio: Son of Abraham and Hagar; ancestor of the Ishmaelites.

name: Stephen
notable_events: Delivered a powerful historical defense of the faith before the Sanhedrin
Saw the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God
Prayed for his executioners as he became the first Christian martyr
short_bio: One of the first deacons in the Jerusalem church and the first Christian martyr.

name: Nicodemus
notable_events: Came to Jesus by night and heard the famous teaching on being “born again”
Brought a generous mixture of seventy-five pounds of myrrh and aloes for Jesus’s burial
short_bio: A Pharisee who sought Jesus' teaching and later aided in his burial.

name: Barnabas
notable_events: Sold property and gave proceeds to apostles
Partnered with Paul on missionary journeys
Advocated for Paul to the Jerusalem church
short_bio: Early Christian leader known for encouragement and missionary work with Paul.

name: Philip the Evangelist
notable_events: Chosen as one of the seven to serve
Preached in Samaria
Baptized the Ethiopian eunuch
short_bio: One of the seven deacons who became a prominent evangelist in Samaria and beyond.

name: Ananias (of Damascus)
notable_events: Sent by the Lord to restore Saul's sight
Baptized Saul (Paul)
short_bio: Disciple in Damascus who obeyed God's call to heal and baptize Saul (Paul).

name: Sapphira
notable_events: Conspired with husband to lie about proceeds
Struck dead after lying to apostles
short_bio: Wife of Ananias (not the Damascus disciple) who died after deceit in the early church.

name: Cornelius
notable_events: Roman centurion described as God-fearing
Received Peter's message and was baptized
Household received the Holy Spirit
short_bio: A Roman centurion whose conversion marked the opening of the church to Gentiles.

name: Timothy
notable_events: Traveled with Paul on missionary journeys
Recipient of two pastoral epistles
Led churches in Ephesus
short_bio: Young leader mentored by Paul who served churches in Asia Minor and received pastoral guidance in epistles.

name: Titus
notable_events: Trusted delegate of Paul
Oversaw church organization in Crete
Recipient of the Epistle to Titus
short_bio: Pauline companion who helped organize churches and received a pastoral epistle.

name: Judas Iscariot
notable_events: Betrayed his Lord Jesus into the hands of the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver
Identified Jesus to the armed mob in the Garden of Gethsemane with a hypocritical kiss
short_bio: One of Jesus' twelve disciples who betrayed him to the authorities.

name: Simon the Zealot
notable_events: Listed among the twelve apostles
Associated with the Zealot movement in some traditions
short_bio: One of the twelve apostles, distinguished in tradition by the title 'the Zealot'.

name: James (brother of Jesus)
notable_events: Brother of Jesus who led the Jerusalem church
Presided at the Jerusalem council
Author of the Epistle of James
short_bio: A leading figure in the early Jerusalem church and author of the Epistle of James.

name: Jairus
notable_events: Sought Jesus to heal his daughter
Witnessed his daughter's resurrection
short_bio: A synagogue leader whose daughter was raised to life by Jesus.

name: Zacchaeus
notable_events: Climbed up into a sycamore-fig tree in Jericho eager to see Jesus passing by
Repented joyfully and gave half his goods to the poor and repaid fraud fourfold
short_bio: A short tax collector who welcomed Jesus and repented, becoming an example of restoration.

name: Good Samaritan
notable_events: Bandaged the wounds of a beaten traveler and paid an innkeeper for his continued care
Was commended by Jesus as the true neighbor who showed boundless mercy
short_bio: The central figure in Jesus' parable who showed mercy to a stranger.

name: Ehud
notable_events: Delivered Israel from Moabite oppression
Assassinated King Eglon
short_bio: Left-handed judge who delivered Israel by killing the Moabite king Eglon.

name: Jethro
occupation: Priest of Midian, father-in-law of Moses
notable_events: Gave Moses counsel on leadership
Visited Moses in the wilderness
short_bio: Priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law who advised him on governing Israel.

name: Epaphroditus
notable_events: Sent by Philippians to assist Paul
Fell ill but recovered
Commended by Paul for service
short_bio: A trusted companion and messenger to Paul from the church at Philippi.

name: Rhoda
notable_events: Answered the door when Peter escaped prison
Ran to tell others but was not believed at first
short_bio: A servant girl who recognized Peter's voice after his miraculous escape from prison.

name: Dodo
notable_events: Named as ancestor in David's mighty men lists
Mentioned in genealogical records
short_bio: A minor figure listed among warriors and genealogies associated with David.

name: Onesimus
notable_events: Runaway slave who became a Christian
Returned to Philemon and was reconciled through Paul's appeal
short_bio: A former slave whose conversion and reconciliation are central to Paul's letter to Philemon.

name: Philemon
notable_events: Recipient of Paul's personal letter
Hosted a church in his home
short_bio: A Christian host and the addressee of Paul's letter concerning Onesimus.

name: Gehazi
notable_events: Served the prophet Elisha
Struck with leprosy for deceit
short_bio: Elisha's servant who was punished with leprosy for greed and deceit.

name: Huldah
notable_events: Consulted about the Book of the Law found in the temple
Delivered a prophetic message to King Josiah's delegation
short_bio: A prophetess who authenticated the Book of the Law and prophesied during Josiah's reforms.

name: Baruch
notable_events: Served as Jeremiah's scribe and companion
Associated with the preservation of Jeremiah's prophecies
short_bio: Jeremiah's scribe who recorded and preserved prophetic messages.

name: Abimelech
occupation: Philistine king; also name of Gideon's son who became king
notable_events: Interacted with Abraham and Isaac over wells
Took a wife from Shechem (Gideon's son Abimelech)
short_bio: Name borne by several rulers in the Bible; notable as a Philistine king and as Abimelech son of Gideon who seized power.

name: Achan
notable_events: Took devoted things at Jericho
Caused Israel's defeat at Ai
Executed for disobedience
short_bio: Israelite who disobeyed God's command at Jericho, bringing judgment on himself and Israel.

name: Adonijah
notable_events: Son of David who attempted to claim the throne
Opposed Solomon's succession
Executed after political intrigue
short_bio: A son of David who sought kingship but was outmaneuvered by Solomon and later put to death.

name: Ahaz
notable_events: Reigned during Assyrian pressure
Introduced idolatrous practices
Sought Assyrian help
short_bio: King of Judah known for unfaithfulness and political alliances with Assyria.

name: Amaziah
notable_events: Defeated Edom
Later turned to idolatry
Assassinated after political turmoil
short_bio: A king of Judah who experienced military success but later fell into idolatry and was overthrown.

name: Asa
notable_events: Reformed the nation early in his reign
Sought the Lord for deliverance
Later relied on foreign alliances
short_bio: King of Judah noted for early reforms and later mixed trust in God and alliances.

name: Athaliah
notable_events: Seized the throne after her son's death
Promoted Baal worship
Overthrown and executed
short_bio: A queen who usurped the throne of Judah and led the nation into idolatry before being removed.

name: Belshazzar
notable_events: Held a profane feast using temple vessels
Saw the writing on the wall
Babylon fell that night
short_bio: Last Babylonian ruler in Daniel's account who witnessed the handwriting predicting Babylon's fall.

name: Bildad
notable_events: One of Job's three friends
Argued that suffering indicates sin
Rebuked by God indirectly through Job's vindication
short_bio: A friend of Job who offered traditional but inadequate explanations for suffering.

name: Zophar
notable_events: One of Job's three friends
Spoke harshly about Job's supposed guilt
Part of the debate on suffering
short_bio: Another of Job's friends who insisted suffering was due to sin and urged repentance.

name: Elihu
notable_events: Intervened in Job's debate after the three friends
Offered a different perspective on suffering
Spoke with passion about God's justice
short_bio: A younger interlocutor in the Book of Job who challenged both Job and his older friends.

name: Mephibosheth
notable_events: Son of Jonathan who was lame in both feet
Shown kindness by David
Restored to David's table
short_bio: Jonathan's son whom David honored, restoring his inheritance and showing covenantal kindness.

name: Shadrach
notable_events: Refused to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's image
Survived the fiery furnace
short_bio: One of three Jewish youths who trusted God and were miraculously preserved in a furnace.

name: Meshach
notable_events: Refused idolatry
Preserved in the fiery furnace with Shadrach and Abednego
short_bio: Companion of Daniel who stood firm in faith and was protected in the furnace.

name: Abednego
notable_events: Refused to worship the golden image
Survived the fiery furnace unharmed
short_bio: One of the three who trusted God rather than bow to idolatry and was miraculously saved.

name: Uriah the Hittite
notable_events: Husband of Bathsheba
Sent to the front and killed on David's orders
short_bio: A loyal soldier whose death was orchestrated by King David after David's adultery with Bathsheba.

name: Jephthah
notable_events: Delivered Israel from Ammonite oppression
Made a tragic vow involving his daughter
short_bio: A judge who secured victory for Israel but whose rash vow brought sorrow to his household.

name: Manoah
notable_events: Received angelic announcement of Samson's birth
Offered sacrifice and sought guidance
short_bio: Father of Samson who encountered an angel announcing his son's Nazirite birth.

name: Delilah
notable_events: Betrayed Samson by discovering the secret of his strength
Instrumental in Samson's capture
short_bio: A Philistine woman who coaxed Samson into revealing his Nazirite secret, leading to his downfall.

name: Abishai
notable_events: Fought alongside David
Killed Abner's men and other enemies
Noted for bravery
short_bio: A valiant warrior in David's service and brother of Joab, known for military exploits.

name: Benaiah
notable_events: Performed daring exploits
Served as commander under David and Solomon
short_bio: A trusted military leader known for courageous deeds and later service under Solomon.

name: Keturah
notable_events: Bore Abraham several sons
Contributed to Abraham's extended lineage
short_bio: A later wife of Abraham who bore him additional children and expanded his family line.

name: Phinehas
notable_events: Acted zealously against idolatry at Peor
Rewarded with a covenant of peace
short_bio: A priest noted for zealous action against idolatry and honored with a lasting covenant.

name: Eliab
notable_events: Present when Samuel came to anoint a king
Initially presumed to be chosen before David was selected
short_bio: Eldest son of Jesse who was overlooked by God when Samuel anointed David as king.

name: Abner
notable_events: Led Israel's forces under Saul
Later allied with David briefly
Assassinated in political strife
short_bio: A powerful military leader in Saul's time who played a key role in the transition to David's rule.

name: Joab
notable_events: Led many of David's military campaigns
Involved in political killings
Executed after Solomon's rise
short_bio: David's military commander, effective but ruthless, whose actions shaped Israel's history.

name: Melchizedek
occupation: King of Salem, priest of God Most High
notable_events: Blessed Abraham
Received tithes from Abraham
Type of priesthood referenced in Psalms and Hebrews
short_bio: Mysterious priest-king who blessed Abraham and serves as a model for Christ's priesthood in the New Testament.

name: Simeon (the devout man)
notable_events: Awaited the consolation of Israel
Blessed the infant Jesus in the temple
short_bio: A devout man who recognized the infant Jesus as the promised consolation and prophesied over him.

name: Anna (prophetess)
notable_events: Served in the temple with fasting and prayer
Recognized and spoke about the child Jesus
short_bio: An elderly prophetess who worshiped in the temple and testified about Jesus to those awaiting redemption.

name: Cleopas
occupation: Disciple on the road to Emmaus
notable_events: Walked with the risen Jesus on the road to Emmaus
Recognized Jesus in the breaking of bread
short_bio: One of the two disciples who encountered the risen Jesus on the road to Emmaus and later reported the experience.

name: Matthias
notable_events: Chosen to replace Judas Iscariot
Selected by lot among the disciples
short_bio: The disciple chosen to fill the vacancy among the twelve apostles after Judas' betrayal.

name: Lydia
notable_events: First European convert recorded in Acts
Hosted Paul and companions in her home
short_bio: A businesswoman from Thyatira whose conversion and hospitality supported Paul's mission in Europe.

name: Priscilla
notable_events: Worked with Aquila in ministry
Instructed Apollos in deeper truth
Hosted a house church
short_bio: A prominent early Christian teacher and missionary who partnered with her husband Aquila in ministry.

name: Aquila
notable_events: Partnered with Paul in tentmaking and ministry
Hosted a church in his home
short_bio: A close coworker of Paul who hosted and supported early Christian gatherings with his wife Priscilla.

name: Apollos
notable_events: Taught accurately about Jesus
Was instructed further by Priscilla and Aquila
Ministered in Corinth and Ephesus
short_bio: An eloquent and knowledgeable teacher who played a significant role in early church instruction and ministry.

name: Sergius Paulus
notable_events: Converted after hearing Paul's message in Cyprus
Opposed by Elymas the sorcerer
short_bio: A Roman official on Cyprus who responded to Paul's preaching and turned to faith.

name: Simon of Cyrene
occupation: Bystander compelled to carry the cross
notable_events: Was compelled by Roman soldiers to carry Jesus’s heavy wooden cross to Golgotha
Is remembered in Mark’s gospel as the father of Alexander and Rufus
short_bio: A passerby compelled to bear Jesus' cross on the way to Golgotha, later remembered by his sons' names.

name: Bartimaeus
notable_events: Called out to Jesus for mercy
Received sight after demonstrating faith
short_bio: A blind man who boldly called to Jesus and was healed, exemplifying persistent faith.

name: Jair
notable_events: Judged Israel for twenty-two years
Had thirty sons who rode thirty donkeys
short_bio: A judge of Israel noted for his household's wealth and influence during his tenure.

name: Nabal
notable_events: Refused David's men hospitality
Saved from David's vengeance by Abigail
Died after learning of his folly
short_bio: A wealthy but foolish man whose refusal to aid David nearly brought disaster on his household until Abigail intervened.

name: Gomer
notable_events: Wife of the prophet Hosea
Her unfaithfulness served as a prophetic symbol of Israel's infidelity
short_bio: Hosea's wife whose life illustrated Israel's unfaithfulness and God's redeeming love.

name: Hosea
notable_events: Prophesied to Israel about unfaithfulness
Used his marriage as a prophetic sign
short_bio: A prophet who used personal and symbolic actions to call Israel back to covenant faithfulness.

name: Nahum
notable_events: Prophesied the fall of Nineveh
Called for justice against Assyrian cruelty
short_bio: A minor prophet who foretold Nineveh's destruction as judgment for its violence.

name: Obadiah
notable_events: Proclaimed judgment against Edom
Called for Israel's vindication
short_bio: Author of a short prophetic book denouncing Edom and affirming God's justice for Israel.

name: Zechariah (prophet)
notable_events: Encouraged rebuilding of the temple
Received apocalyptic visions
short_bio: A post-exilic prophet who encouraged restoration and offered visions pointing to future hope.

name: Malachi
notable_events: Called Israel to faithfulness after the exile
Addressed issues of worship and justice
short_bio: The final book of the Old Testament, calling God's people to renewed covenantal faithfulness.

name: Andrew
notable_events: First called by Jesus
Brought Peter to Jesus
short_bio: Brother of Peter and one of the first disciples called by Jesus.

name: James son of Alphaeus
notable_events: Listed among the Twelve
short_bio: One of the Twelve apostles, distinguished from James son of Zebedee.

name: Thaddaeus
notable_events: Asked Jesus why He would reveal Himself to the disciples and not the world
short_bio: One of the Twelve apostles, also called Jude or Lebbaeus.

name: Bartholomew
notable_events: Called an Israelite without deceit
Recognized Jesus as Son of God
short_bio: A sincere seeker who became one of the Twelve apostles, also known as Nathanael.

name: Philip (the Apostle)
notable_events: Brought Nathanael to Jesus
Asked Jesus to show the Father
short_bio: One of the Twelve apostles known for inviting others to meet Jesus.

name: Thomas
notable_events: Insisted he would not believe the resurrection without seeing the nail marks in Jesus’s hands
Worshipfully proclaimed Jesus as “My Lord and my God!” upon touching His wounds
short_bio: Apostle known for his honest doubt and later profound confession of faith.

name: Silas
notable_events: Imprisoned with Paul in Philippi
Helped deliver letters to churches
short_bio: A leading member of the early church who traveled with Paul on missionary journeys.

name: John Mark
notable_events: Traveled with Paul and Barnabas
Author of the Gospel of Mark
short_bio: Companion of Paul and Barnabas and traditionally regarded as the author of the Gospel of Mark.

name: Simeon called Niger
notable_events: Part of the leadership team in Antioch
short_bio: A leader in the multicultural Antioch church who helped commission Paul and Barnabas.

name: Lucius of Cyrene
notable_events: Helped lead the Antioch church
short_bio: One of the prophets and teachers in the Antioch church who supported early missions.

name: Manaen
notable_events: Brought up with Herod Antipas
Leader in Antioch church
short_bio: A prominent believer raised with Herod Antipas who became a leader in the Antioch church.

name: Agabus
notable_events: Predicted a famine
Foretold Paul's arrest
short_bio: A prophet in the early church known for accurate predictions about famine and Paul's imprisonment.

name: Eutychus
notable_events: Fell from a window during Paul's sermon
Raised back to life
short_bio: A young man who fell asleep during Paul's preaching and was miraculously restored to life.

name: Trophimus
notable_events: Accompanied Paul on journeys
Illness prevented him from traveling
short_bio: An Ephesian believer who traveled with Paul and is mentioned in several letters.

name: Aristarchus
notable_events: Dragged into the Ephesian riot
Traveled with Paul to Rome
short_bio: A Macedonian believer who endured hardship with Paul and traveled with him to Rome.

name: Sopater
notable_events: Traveled with Paul through Asia
short_bio: A Berean believer who accompanied Paul on his travels and supported his ministry.

name: Jason
notable_events: Sheltered Paul and Silas
Dragged before city officials
short_bio: A Thessalonian believer who risked his safety to host Paul and Silas during persecution.

name: Stephanas
notable_events: First convert in Achaia
Devoted to serving the saints
short_bio: A respected early convert whose household was known for dedicated service to the church.

name: Phoebe
notable_events: Carrier of the letter to the Romans
Helper of many believers
short_bio: A deacon and benefactor in the early church who delivered Paul's letter to the Romans.

name: Chloe
notable_events: Her household reported divisions in Corinth
short_bio: A respected woman whose household informed Paul about issues in the Corinthian church.

name: Erastus
notable_events: Held a civic office in Corinth
Associated with Paul
short_bio: A high-ranking official in Corinth who supported Paul's ministry.

name: Crispus
notable_events: Believed in the Lord with his household
short_bio: A synagogue leader in Corinth who converted under Paul's preaching.

name: Sosthenes
notable_events: Beaten before Gallio
Later greeted as a brother in Christ
short_bio: A synagogue leader who later became a believer and co-sender of 1 Corinthians.

name: Gallio
notable_events: Dismissed charges against Paul
short_bio: A Roman governor who refused to prosecute Paul, setting a legal precedent for early Christians.

name: Elymas
notable_events: Opposed Paul and Barnabas
Struck blind temporarily
short_bio: A false prophet who opposed the gospel and was struck blind by Paul’s rebuke.

name: Demetrius the Silversmith
notable_events: Started a riot in Ephesus over idol trade
short_bio: A craftsman who incited a riot against Paul to protect the idol-making industry in Ephesus.

name: Alexander the Coppersmith
notable_events: Opposed Paul strongly
short_bio: A metalworker who caused Paul significant harm and opposed his ministry.

name: Onesiphorus
notable_events: Refreshed Paul in prison
Sought him out in Rome
short_bio: A faithful believer who encouraged Paul during imprisonment and served the church sacrificially.

name: Tychicus
notable_events: Delivered letters for Paul
Encouraged churches
short_bio: A trusted messenger who carried Paul’s letters and strengthened early churches.
